job.title: Procurement Business Partner
job.description:
Procurement Business Partner

Location: Bankstown, Sydney NSW
Salary: Commencing from $108,644 + 12% superannuation, with higher remuneration available for suitably experienced and highly qualified candidates
Work Type: Full Time, Permanent
Public Sector People on behalf of Canterbury-Bankstown Council

Become a trusted Procurement Business Partner across one of NSW's largest councils, delivering end-to-end sourcing activities, providing practical advice and supporting stakeholders to achieve effective, compliant and value-for-money procurement outcomes.

Public Sector People are proud to partner with Canterbury-Bankstown Council to recruit three Procurement Business Partners within its Corporate Directorate.

These opportunities offer experienced procurement professionals the chance to work closely with managers, people leaders and project teams across Council,  understanding business needs, influencing procurement decisions and supporting forward procurement planning across a diverse range of categories and services.

You'll play an important role in helping stakeholders navigate procurement processes, manage risk and make informed decisions, while contributing to improved procurement capability and service delivery across the organisation.

You will also contribute to Council's evolving procurement function, helping establish a more proactive, collaborative and customer focused approach to procurement.

This is a role for someone who enjoys working with people, can confidently provide practical procurement advice and takes a proactive, solutions-focused approach to achieving outcomes.
  
About the Role

Reporting to the Procurement Operations Lead, you will be responsible for:
  • Lead and coordinate end-to-end sourcing and procurement activities across a diverse range of categories and Council services.
  • Partner with managers, people leaders and project teams to understand procurement requirements, anticipate future needs, support forward procurement planning and deliver effective outcomes.
  • Develop fit-for-purpose procurement strategies and sourcing approaches that deliver value for money and effective commercial outcomes.
  • Provide practical advice on procurement processes, governance, probity and compliance requirements.
  • Support stakeholders in developing procurement approaches that achieve value for money and manage commercial risk, including market analysis and evaluation of sourcing options.
  • Identify and manage procurement-related risks, ensuring appropriate controls and mitigation strategies are in place.
  • Build procurement capability across Council through training, coaching and practical guidance to stakeholders, including supporting the development of clear, fit-for-purpose specifications, procurement documentation and sourcing requirements.
  • Identify opportunities to improve procurement processes, systems and ways of working and contribute to the ongoing development of Council's procurement service delivery model.
  • Develop strong stakeholder relationships, promoting a collaborative and customer-focused approach to procurement.
  
What You'll Bring
  • Demonstrated experience delivering end-to-end procurement and contract lifecycle activities within government or a complex organisational environment.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills, with the ability to build trust, influence decisions and provide practical advice.
  • Sound understanding of procurement governance, probity, compliance and risk management.
  • Strong commercial acumen, including experience developing procurement strategies, evaluating sourcing options and negotiating commercial outcomes.
  • Strong communication, negotiation and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work collaboratively across different business areas.
  • A proactive and solutions-focused approach, with the ability to manage competing priorities and take ownership of procurement activities.
  • Experience using procurement systems and digital technologies, with an interest in continuous improvement.
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications or equivalent extensive experience.
 
Why Canterbury-Bankstown Council?
  • Work across a diverse range of procurement categories, projects and Council services.
  • Build strong stakeholder relationships and become a trusted procurement advisor.
  • Help shape Council's evolving procurement business partnering model and contribute to a more proactive and commercially focused procurement function.
  • Join one of NSW's largest and growing councils, contributing to projects and services that make a meaningful impact on the community.
  • Enjoy a range of Local Government benefits, including hybrid working, Scheduled Days Off (SDOs), learning and development opportunities, and health and wellbeing programs, all from a convenient Bankstown location close to the train station.
Ready to Make an Impact?

Contact Esme Lynch at Public Sector People on 0413 282 765 or email esme@publicsectorpeople.com.au for a confidential discussion.

Applications close 11:59pm, Sunday 8th November 2026, please note recruitment activity will commence prior to the closing date.

job.title: Strategic Procurement and Contracts Lead
job.description:
Strategic Procurement and Contracts Lead

Location: Bankstown, Sydney NSW
Salary: Commencing from $131,278 + 12% superannuation, with higher remuneration available for suitably experienced and highly qualified candidates
Work Type: Full Time, Permanent
Public Sector People on behalf of Canterbury-Bankstown Council
  
Lead complex, high-value procurement and contract management activities, providing strategic advice and influencing commercial decisions, contract performance and procurement outcomes across one of NSW's largest councils.

Public Sector People are proud to partner with Canterbury-Bankstown Council to recruit two Strategic Procurement and Contracts Leads within its Corporate Directorate.

These opportunities will suit experienced strategic procurement and contract management professionals who enjoy navigating complex contractual matters, influencing stakeholders and delivering effective procurement outcomes across a diverse range of Council services and projects.

You'll act as a trusted subject matter expert on significant procurement and contract matters, working closely with senior stakeholders, project managers and business units to strengthen decision-making, manage risk and improve contract performance.

You will also contribute to Council's evolving procurement function, strengthening strategic sourcing, contract management governance and commercial capability across the organisation.

This is a role for someone who combines strong technical procurement expertise with sound commercial judgement, strategic thinking and the confidence to provide clear, practical advice on complex matters.

About the Role

Reporting to the Manager Procurement, you will be responsible for:
  • Lead end-to-end strategic procurement activities across high-value, high-risk and complex projects and programs, including developing sourcing strategies, undertaking market analysis and identifying opportunities to achieve value for money.
  • Lead the development, implementation and ongoing improvement of Council's contract management framework, including governance requirements, performance monitoring, reporting and guidance for contract owners.
  • Provide specialist procurement and contractual advice on major contracts, including negotiation, risk allocation and contract execution.
  • Lead the establishment and management of procurement panels, ensuring effective utilisation and value-for-money outcomes, including identifying opportunities to improve procurement efficiency and leverage Council's purchasing arrangements.
  • Strengthen contract management governance across Council, providing specialist oversight and advice on supplier performance, KPIs, contract variations, extensions, disputes and contractual obligations.
  • Oversee contract governance and performance, including supplier performance, KPIs, variations, extensions and disputes.
  • Partner with project managers and senior stakeholders to develop effective procurement strategies, manage contractual obligations and mitigate risk, providing expert advice on complex commercial and contractual matters.
  • Contribute to the development and improvement of procurement strategies, policies, frameworks and contract management systems, supporting consistent and effective contract management practices across Council.
  • Analyse procurement and contract data to identify risks, trends and opportunities for continuous improvement.
  • Build procurement and contract management capability across Council through specialist training, coaching and practical guidance, supporting stakeholders and contract managers to understand contractual obligations, manage supplier performance and address commercial risks.
  • Provide specialist advice and support to Procurement Business Partners and other procurement professionals on complex sourcing strategies, and contractual matters
What You'll Bring
  • Extensive experience in strategic procurement and contract lifecycle management within a complex or regulated organisational environment.
  • Demonstrated experience leading high-value, high-risk and complex procurement activities, including major contracts and procurement panels, with a proven ability to develop sourcing strategies and deliver effective commercial outcomes.
  • Strong procurement and contractual expertise, including negotiation, contract performance, risk management and dispute resolution.
  • Sound understanding of procurement governance, probity and legislative compliance requirements.
  • Demonstrated experience leading, developing or improving contract management frameworks, governance practices and supplier performance arrangements.
  • Highly developed stakeholder engagement skills, with the confidence to provide specialist advice and influence senior decision-makers.
  • Sound commercial acumen, strategic thinking and problem-solving capabilities, with the ability to deliver practical procurement and contractual solutions.
  • Experience using contract management systems and contributing to procurement and governance improvements.
  • Experience building organisational capability through specialist advice, training and coaching in procurement and contract management practices.
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications or equivalent extensive experience.
Why Canterbury-Bankstown Council?
  • Lead complex procurement and contract management activities across a diverse portfolio of Council services and projects.
  • Influence strategic procurement decisions and provide trusted procurement and contract management advice to senior stakeholders.
  • Be part of one of NSW's largest and growing councils, contributing to projects and services that make a meaningful impact on the community.
  • Help shape Council's evolving procurement function, strengthening strategic sourcing, commercial capability and contract management practices across the organisation.
  • Enjoy a range of Local Government benefits, including hybrid working, Scheduled Days Off (SDOs), learning and development opportunities, and health and wellbeing programs, all from a convenient Bankstown location close to the train station.
Ready to Make an Impact?

job.title: Mechanical Draftsperson
job.description:
Mechanical Draftsperson HVAC
Dandenong South, VIC
Salary: $100,000–$115,000 + Super
Location: South Melbourne, Melbourne
Type: Full-time, On-site

The Opportunity Our client is a well-established Tier 2 mechanical and electrical contractor delivering commercial, industrial and technically complex building services projects across Melbourne.

Due to continued growth, they are seeking a Mechanical Draftsperson to join their team in Dandenong South. This is an excellent opportunity for a technically capable drafter with experience in HVAC and mechanical building services to work closely with project managers, engineers and site teams, producing accurate drawings that support project delivery from design through to construction.

The successful candidate will play an important role in coordinating mechanical services, resolving design clashes and ensuring drawings are practical, accurate and ready for installation.
Key Responsibilities
  • Produce detailed mechanical services drawings, including HVAC ductwork, pipework, plant layouts and associated building services.
  • Prepare mechanical shop drawings, fabrication drawings and construction documentation.
  • Coordinate mechanical designs with electrical, hydraulic, structural and other building services disciplines.
  • Identify and resolve design clashes and constructability issues before works commence on site.
  • Interpret engineering designs, specifications and project documentation to develop accurate drawings.
  • Update drawings to reflect design changes, site conditions and project requirements.
  • Prepare as-built drawings and maintain accurate drawing registers and document control.
  • Liaise with project managers, engineers, subcontractors and site personnel to support efficient project delivery.
  • Ensure drawings comply with relevant Australian Standards, project specifications and installation requirements.
About You To be successful in this role, you will ideally have:
  • Previous experience as a Mechanical Draftsperson, HVAC Draftsperson or Mechanical Services Drafter.
  • Experience within commercial construction, mechanical contracting or building services.
  • Strong knowledge of HVAC systems, including ductwork, pipework and mechanical plant layouts.
  • Proficiency in AutoCAD, with Revit and BIM coordination experience highly regarded.
  • The ability to interpret engineering drawings, specifications and technical documentation.
  • A strong understanding of construction sequencing, coordination and practical installation requirements.
  • Excellent attention to detail, organisational skills and the ability to manage competing deadlines.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively with project and site teams.
What's on Offer?
  • Competitive salary of $100,000–$115,000 + Super.
  • A stable, full-time opportunity with an established Tier 2 contractor.
  • Exposure to a diverse range of commercial and technically challenging projects.
  • A collaborative team environment with close involvement in project delivery.
  • The opportunity to further develop your technical drafting and coordination capabilities.
Apply Now If you are an experienced Mechanical Draftsperson looking for your next opportunity within the Melbourne building services market, we would like to hear from you.
For a confidential discussion, apply now or contact Design & Build to find out more about the role.

job.title: Manager Community Safety
job.description:
About Strathbogie Shire Council

Strathbogie Shire Council is a progressive regional municipality encompassing communities including Euroa, Nagambie, Avenel and Violet Town, ideally positioned between Melbourne and Shepparton.

Council is committed to delivering responsive, consistent and customer focused services that support community safety, regulatory compliance and the amenity of the Shire. With a diverse rural landscape and a broad range of services, Council plays an important role in supporting residents, businesses and communities across the municipality.

This is an opportunity to build on significant service improvements, strengthen team capability and shape how community safety and regulatory services operate within a regional council, with practical opportunities to improve the experience of the community.

About the Role

Reporting to the Director Community & Planning, the Manager Community Safety will lead a diverse portfolio spanning local laws, community compliance, animal management, environmental health, building, planning compliance and emergency management.

This is a broad leadership position with responsibility for service delivery, legislative compliance, people leadership and continuous improvement across several interconnected functions. You will oversee day-to-day operations, support and develop a multidisciplinary team, manage resources and budgets, and ensure services are delivered consistently and effectively.

A key priority will be to oversee the implementation of Council’s new local law, embedding clear processes and supporting consistent application across the municipality. You will also drive practical improvements to regulatory services, including streamlining permitting processes, strengthening customer communication and identifying opportunities to improve efficiency and accessibility for residents and businesses.

You will build on work already undertaken to review services, systems and team structures, establishing clear accountabilities, effective reporting and a positive, accountable team culture. The role will also provide leadership across emergency management and recovery, supporting Council’s preparedness, response and recovery responsibilities.

Working closely with the Director, Councillors, staff, community members, businesses and external service providers, you will provide sound advice on complex regulatory matters, manage sensitive complaints and ensure legislative obligations are met. This is an opportunity to balance operational leadership with longer-term service development and make a tangible difference to how Council supports its community.
  
About You

You are an experienced regulatory services or community safety leader who brings sound judgement, strong people leadership and a practical approach to improving services. You understand the importance of balancing legislative requirements with responsive, accessible customer service, and can navigate complex matters involving competing stakeholder interests and community expectations.

You bring experience interpreting and applying legislation, developing policies and procedures, and leading change across a multidisciplinary team. You are comfortable managing operational priorities, budgets and resources while identifying opportunities to simplify processes, strengthen accountability and deliver better outcomes.

Just as importantly, you are a calm, measured and approachable leader who builds trust, sets clear expectations and supports people to perform at their best. You can have difficult conversations when required, address performance constructively and foster a culture of professionalism, collaboration and continuous improvement.

You are confident engaging with a broad range of stakeholders, from residents and local businesses through to Councillors, senior leaders and external agencies. You bring the ability to make considered decisions on sensitive issues, communicate clearly and maintain a focus on fair, consistent and defensible outcomes.

Experience across every service area is not essential, what matters is your ability to lead across a varied portfolio, apply sound judgement and build your knowledge where needed. An understanding of emergency management, business continuity and disaster recovery will be important, alongside a genuine interest in the opportunities and practical challenges of working within a rural municipality.

Most importantly, you are motivated by the opportunity to lead a broad and meaningful portfolio, build on existing improvements and help shape a capable, connected and customer focused community safety function.

Application Process

Public Sector People is partnering with Strathbogie Shire Council to recruit this important leadership opportunity.

For a confidential discussion or to request a copy of the Position Description, please contact;

Marcel Lafontaine – marcel@publicsectorpeople.com.au - 0423 668 753
Sarah Kettlewell – sarah@publicsectorpeople.com.au – 0478 041 199

To apply, please submit your CV and a brief cover letter via the link.

Applications close Wednesday 11 November 2026

This role will be responsible for ensuring incoming structural steel, fabricated components and prefabricated modules meet project specifications, tolerances and quality standards. A key focus will be managing the Inspection and Test Plan (ITP) process and ensuring quality procedures are consistently followed by the entire project team.

Key Responsibilities

  • Identify quality risks and implement improvements to prevent defects, rework and delays.
To be successful in this role, you will have:
  • Experience in quality assurance within structural steel, prefabrication, modular construction or a related engineering environment.
  • A background in structural engineering, fabrication or quality inspection.
  • Strong understanding of ITPs, inspection processes, dimensional checks and engineering tolerances.
  • Ability to interpret engineering drawings, specifications and quality documentation.
  • Strong attention to detail and confidence coordinating quality requirements across multiple teams.
  • A proactive approach to identifying issues, driving corrective actions and maintaining quality standards.

You will have the opportunity to put your mark on significant strategy work and build achievements with lasting value for the city. The team offers a supportive environment with high standards, shared expertise and room to develop your career.

job.title: Project Engineer - Electrical
job.description:
Project Engineer – Electrical
Location: Kings Park, NSW
Salary: $120,000 – $170,000 + Super, depending on experience
Employment Type: Full-Time, Permanent

This role would suit an electrically qualified engineer who enjoys working across technical design, project coordination and engineering delivery.

With opportunities available at both Project Engineer and Senior Project Engineer level, this is an excellent opportunity to join a technical team where you can take ownership of projects, work closely with key stakeholders and contribute to the delivery of high-quality electrical solutions.

Working closely with the engineering and project teams, your responsibilities will include:
  • As a Project Engineer you will be coordinating electrical engineering projects from initial design through to delivery and commissioning.
  • This Project Engineer will be preparing, reviewing and interpreting electrical drawings, schematics and technical documentation.
  • Utilising AutoCAD to develop, review and modify electrical designs.
  • The Project Engineer will be working on generator systems, switchboards, switchgear and associated electrical infrastructure.
  • As a Project Engineer you'll be reviewing electrical calculations, including fault current, overload protection and cable sizing.
  • The Project Engineer will be supporting the selection, integration and specification of electrical equipment.
  • As the Project Engineer you'll consider acoustic requirements and other technical constraints as part of equipment and system design.
  • This Project Engineer will be liaising with clients, suppliers, contractors and internal stakeholders to ensure projects meet technical and commercial requirements.
For a more senior appointment, you will also take on greater responsibility for technical leadership, project oversight and supporting the Head of Department with the coordination and development of the engineering team.

About You To be successful in this role, you will ideally have:
  • A degree in Electrical Engineering or a strong electrical engineering background.
  • Experience in electrical project engineering within a manufacturing, power generation, MEP or electrical infrastructure environment.
  • Exposure to generators, ideally brands such as Caterpillar (CAT), Cummins or Perkins, or experience with switchboards and switchgear.
  • Proficiency in AutoCAD and the ability to interpret and produce electrical drawings.
  • The ability to coordinate multiple technical requirements and work effectively across disciplines.
  • Strong communication skills and the confidence to liaise with clients, suppliers and internal teams.
  • A practical, solutions-focused approach to engineering challenges.
  • A stable employment history, demonstrating commitment and a genuine interest in developing a long-term career.
  • Experience in MEP environments with a strong electrical focus will also be highly regarded.
  • Project Engineer: $120,000 – $140,000 + Super, with some flexibility for the right candidate.
  • Senior Project Engineer / 2IC: $150,000 – $170,000 + Super, with scope for a highly experienced applicant.
Apply Now If you are an Electrical Engineer with experience in power generation, industrial, switchgear or electrical building services, we'd like to hear from you.

To be successful, you will ideally have:

job.title: Project Manager

A highly regarded Sydney construction business with a strong reputation for delivering high-quality residential, commercial and hospitality projects, including complex refurbishments and adaptive re-use developments.

Known for their hands-on leadership, collaborative approach and commitment to quality, the business has established strong relationships with clients, consultants and subcontractors.

An excellent opportunity exists for an experienced Project Manager to join a respected Sydney builder and take responsibility for overseeing a $40M boutique class 2 development in Sydney's inner West.

Working closely with the senior leadership team, you will have overall responsibility for the successful delivery of the project, ensuring it is delivered safely, on time, within budget and to the highest quality standards.

This role will suit a capable Project Manager who is comfortable managing multiple projects simultaneously, balancing competing priorities and leading separate project teams while maintaining strong commercial and operational oversight.

The Role

  • Developing, managing and monitoring construction programs and key milestones
  • Maintaining control of project budgets, forecasting and commercial performance
  • Overseeing procurement, subcontractor negotiations and contract administration
  • Managing consultants, subcontractors, clients and key project stakeholders
  • Coordinating design development and resolving construction and buildability challenges
  • Identifying project risks and implementing effective mitigation strategies
  • Monitoring site progress, productivity and quality across both projects
  • Maintaining high standards of WHS, quality assurance and compliance
  • Providing regular project reporting and updates to senior management
  • Driving projects through practical completion, defects and final handover
About You
  • Proven experience as a Project Manager within the Australian construction industry
  • Strong background delivering residential, commercial or mixed-use construction projects
  • Strong commercial acumen and understanding of contracts, procurement and cost control
  • Excellent programming, planning and organisational capabilities
  • Proven ability to lead multiple project teams and coordinate subcontractors effectively
  • Strong communication, negotiation and stakeholder management skills
  • Degree qualified in Construction Management, Engineering or a related discipline
  • A proactive, hands-on approach with the ability to work autonomously and make informed decisions
In Return
  • Salary up to $250,000 + Super, depending on experience
  • Join a respected Sydney builder delivering high-quality construction projects
  • Work closely with an experienced and hands-on senior leadership team
  • Genuine autonomy and responsibility across multiple projects
  • Exposure to technically interesting residential and commercial construction
  • Supportive and collaborative team environment
  • Strong pipeline of upcoming projects offering long-term career stability
  • Opportunities for continued professional development and career progression
How to Apply

 Click Apply and include your CV/resume and project list (Word format preferred).

For a confidential discussion about this opportunity, contact Mitchell Barker on 0423 927 536.

All applications will be treated with strict confidentiality.

job.title: Business Analyst
job.description:
We are seeking an experienced Business Analyst to support the delivery of key business and technology initiatives across the organisation.
  
Working with a range of stakeholders, this role will focus on analysing business problems, understanding desired outcomes, and defining what success looks like before solutions are implemented. The discovery work has largely been completed, and the council is now seeking a BA who can work through the problem space, assess impacts, identify opportunities, and establish clear target-state outcomes that technology can ultimately enable.
  
The successful candidate will act as the bridge between business and technology teams, ensuring initiatives remain outcome-focused and aligned to organisational objectives. This is an excellent opportunity for a Business Analyst who enjoys working at a strategic level, helping stakeholders define tangible business benefits, measurable outcomes, and a clear vision for future-state operations.
  
Key Responsibilities
  • Analyse complex business challenges and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Facilitate stakeholder workshops to understand business objectives, pain points and desired outcomes.
  • Define future-state processes, business capabilities and success measures.
  • Gather, document and validate business, functional and non-functional requirements.
  • Develop business cases, process maps, impact assessments and recommendations.
  • Conduct options analysis and support informed decision-making.
  • Ensure technology initiatives remain aligned to business objectives and strategic outcomes.
  • Work closely with project managers, technical teams and business stakeholders throughout delivery.
  • Support business readiness, testing and implementation activities.
  • Build strong relationships across operational, leadership and technical stakeholder groups.
  
Essential Experience & Skills
  • Demonstrated experience as a Business Analyst within complex business, ICT or transformation environments.
  • Strong capability in business process analysis, problem definition and outcome-focused requirements gathering.
  • Proven ability to facilitate workshops and engage stakeholders at all levels.
  • Experience defining target-state outcomes, benefits and success metrics.
  • Strong analytical, documentation and communication skills.
  • Ability to challenge assumptions and help stakeholders clearly articulate desired business outcomes.
  • Experience working across both business and technology teams.
  • Strong stakeholder management and relationship-building skills.
  
Desirable Experience
  • Business transformation or organisational change initiatives.
  • Process improvement and service redesign projects.
  • Enterprise systems and technology-enabled business change.
  • Local Government or public sector environments.
  • Data, reporting or information management projects.
  • Agile, Hybrid or Waterfall delivery methodologies.
  
Preferred Qualifications
  • Tertiary qualification in Business Analysis, Business Management, Information Technology, Information Systems or a related discipline.
  
If you are keen to apply, please apply with a WORD copy of your CV
   
If you would like to discuss this role in more detail or other IT opportunities within Local, State or Federal Government, please contact:
  
Callum Bowie
  
cbowie@publicsectorpeople.com.au

job.title: Director - Program Operational Continuity
job.description:
Public Sector People is recruiting an experienced Director – Program Operational Continuity (SO3) to join a major Queensland Government organisation delivering a large-scale operational program.

This is a senior leadership opportunity to influence long-term operational strategy, overseeing critical infrastructure, facilities, fleet, logistics and digital solutions across a complex and geographically dispersed service network.

About the Role

Reporting into senior executive leadership you will provide strategic direction across essential operational support functions, ensuring the organisation has the infrastructure, resources and systems required to achieve its objectives.

A significant focus of this position will be reviewing the organisation's existing depot network and developing a comprehensive estate strategy to support operational requirements through to 2032.

You will work closely with executive stakeholders and operational leaders to identify opportunities for improvement, strengthen service delivery and ensure resources are aligned with evolving operational requirements.

This position is classified at the SO3 level with an indicative hourly rate of $110 – $125 per hour + super dependent on experience and the applicable Queensland Government remuneration benchmarks.


Key Responsibilities
  • Provide strategic leadership across facilities, fleet, logistics, data and digital solutions.
  • Lead a comprehensive review of the organisation's depot footprint, considering operational requirements, workforce distribution, leases and safety.
  • Develop and implement a long-term estate strategy supporting operational delivery through to 2032.
  • Provide high-level strategic advice to executive leadership on operational continuity, infrastructure planning and resource allocation.
  • Drive improvements in operational efficiency, governance, service delivery and organisational performance.
  • Manage complex stakeholder relationships across government, operational teams and external service providers.
  • Lead organisational change and continuous improvement initiatives.
About You

We are seeking an experienced senior leader with a demonstrated ability to manage complex, multidisciplinary functions within large organisations.

The successful candidate will demonstrate:
  • Significant leadership experience at Director or equivalent senior management level.
  • Strong experience in strategic operations, infrastructure planning, facilities management, logistics or asset management.
  • Proven ability to develop and implement long-term operational strategies across geographically dispersed operations.
  • Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and managing complex stakeholder relationships.
  • Strong commercial acumen, governance capability and financial management experience.
  • Demonstrated success delivering organisational change, operational improvements and strategic projects.
  • Experience within government, large-scale infrastructure, utilities or similarly complex operational environments will be highly regarded.
  • Relevant tertiary qualification (Degree/Diploma/Associate Diploma) or equivalent in a related field.
Why Apply?

This opportunity offers the chance to contribute to a significant Queensland Government program with substantial operational complexity and long-term strategic importance.

You will play a central role in shaping the organisation's operational infrastructure and future service delivery capability, working alongside senior decision-makers to deliver meaningful improvements.

How to Apply

If you are an experienced senior leader with a background in strategic operations, infrastructure or complex program delivery, we encourage you to apply.

Please submit your CV in WORD format

This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced Asset Management professional to lead a small, capable team while driving the continual improvement of Council's asset management capability across one of NSW's largest local government areas.

You'll play a key role in shaping how Council plans, manages and invests in its infrastructure, improving the quality of asset data, embedding consistent practices across the organisation and helping deliver smarter, data-driven capital investment decisions.

The Opportunity

You'll lead the ongoing implementation of Council's Asset Management Improvement Plan, continue improving systems and processes, and help build a consistent approach to asset planning across a diverse infrastructure portfolio.

Working alongside Finance and operational teams, you'll ensure asset information supports long-term planning, renewal programs, capital investment decisions and future service delivery.

You'll also lead a team of Asset Management professionals, providing guidance, mentoring and direction while fostering a culture of continuous improvement.

It's a rare opportunity to combine leadership, strategic thinking, systems improvement and hands-on asset management in one role.

About You
We're looking for someone who enjoys improving systems, solving complex problems and helping organisations make better infrastructure decisions.

You'll ideally bring:
  • Experience in infrastructure asset management, asset planning or strategic asset management.
  • Experience developing or improving Asset Management Plans and asset management frameworks.
  • Strong analytical capability with confidence working with large datasets and asset information.

With more than five years of work expected across the development, this is an excellent opportunity to join a project with long-term continuity, take ownership of key commercial packages and play an important role in protecting project margins and progress internally to a Project Manager level.

This is a commercially focused role suited to someone who understands the importance of contractual risk, proactive procurement and cost control, and who enjoys taking ownership of commercial outcomes rather than simply administering contracts.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Managing head contract and subcontract administration across a major Class 2 residential apartment development.
  • Preparing, reviewing and issuing subcontract agreements, scopes of work and contractual documentation.
  • Managing variations, progress claims, payment schedules and subcontractor payments.
  • Monitoring project costs, forecasting expenditure and maintaining accurate budget reporting.
  • Leading procurement activities and negotiating with subcontractors and suppliers to achieve favourable commercial outcomes.
  • Identifying contractual risks, cost exposures and opportunities to maximise project profitability.
  • Reviewing contract terms, managing notices and ensuring contractual obligations and deadlines are met.
  • Supporting value engineering, risk management and commercial negotiations alongside the Project Manager.
  • Maintaining strong relationships with subcontractors, consultants and project stakeholders while confidently managing difficult commercial conversations.
  • Maintaining accurate project records and supporting the successful delivery of the project through to completion.
About You:
  • Minimum 2+ years' experience as a Contracts Administrator within the Australian construction industry.
  • Previous experience delivering Class 2 residential apartment projects, ideally valued at $30M+.
  • Strong understanding of Australian standard-form construction contracts, including AS4000 and AS2124, or equivalent relevant contract experience.
  • A solid understanding of subcontract procurement, variations, progress claims, cost reporting and commercial risk management.
  • Commercially minded, with the ability to identify contractual opportunities and protect project margins.
  • A proactive problem-solver who can think critically, work independently and take ownership of challenges.
  • Confident communicating with subcontractors and stakeholders, including managing difficult conversations and negotiating commercial outcomes.
  • Strong organisational skills, attention to detail and the ability to manage competing deadlines.
What's On Offer / Salary Package:
  • Salary package of approximately $150K–$250K, depending on experience and capability.
  • Opportunity to work on a major $110M residential apartment development.
  • More than five years of anticipated project work, offering excellent continuity and long-term career stability.
  • The opportunity to work within a commercially driven business that places genuine importance on contractual knowledge, risk management and project profitability.
  • Exposure to complex contracts, significant subcontract packages and the full commercial lifecycle of a major development.
  • Strong training, mentorship and career progression opportunities, with a demonstrated commitment to developing future Project Managers and senior commercial leaders.
  • Join a collaborative project team with a strong focus on quality, safety, contractual compliance and commercial performance.
If you're a commercially driven Contracts Administrator or Senior Contracts Administrator looking to take the next step in your career, this is an excellent opportunity to join a reputable builder on a major multi-stage development with long-term work in Wollongong.

job.title: Manager Communities & Cultural Services
job.description:
Manager Community & Cultural Services
Central Highlands Regional Council | Emerald, QLD | $210K–$252K TRP
  
Public Sector People is partnering with Central Highlands Regional Council to appoint a Manager Community & Cultural Services, an influential leadership role based in Emerald.
  
An opportunity to lead, influence and make a difference.
  
Take ownership of a broad portfolio of services that matter to communities across the Central Highlands, with the freedom to develop people, strengthen performance and shape future priorities.
  
Council is seeking a confident, practical leader who can bring teams together, solve complex problems and turn strategic direction into tangible results.
  
With key initiatives underway, you will build on established foundations, strengthen governance and capability, and make a lasting contribution to the organisation and its communities.
  
The Opportunity
  
Reporting to the Director Communities, you will lead libraries, arts and culture, community grants, regional events, youth programs, First Nations initiatives, community relationships and human and social recovery.
  
This varied portfolio calls for a leader who can connect different functions, set clear priorities and deliver outcomes. You do not need to be a technical specialist in every service area; strong leadership and good governance are essential.
  
Your key responsibilities will include:
  • Providing strategic and operational leadership across the Community and Cultural Services portfolio
  • Coaching and developing multidisciplinary teams and strengthening accountability and performance
  • Improving the quality and effectiveness of community programs and public-facing services
  • Progressing strategies and initiatives across libraries, arts, culture and heritage
  • Overseeing community grants and aligning programs with Council and community priorities
  • Managing budgets, resources, service performance and financial accountability
  • Building partnerships with community organisations, Traditional Owners and government agencies
  • Providing considered advice to the Executive Leadership Team and elected representatives
  • Strengthening governance, systems, planning and operational processes
  • Identifying practical opportunities for innovation and measurable community outcomes
About You
  
Above all, you will be a capable people leader who gets results.
  
You will thrive in a complex service environment, communicate clearly, navigate competing priorities and bring people with you through change while setting high expectations.
  
Ideally, you will bring:
  
  • Proven leadership experience in government, community services or a complex service organisation
  • Experience managing multidisciplinary teams and building capability in others
  • Good governance, financial management and operational planning skills
  • Ability to translate strategy into practical programs and measurable outcomes
  • Strong communication, negotiation and stakeholder engagement capability
  • Confidence working with executives, elected representatives and diverse communities
  • Sound judgement and an ability to manage competing expectations and priorities
  • Experience delivering positive community outcomes and service improvements
  • A collaborative, practical approach to change and continuous improvement
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications and/or substantial comparable leadership experience
Council welcomes candidates from local and state government, major not-for-profit organisations and other community-focused service providers. A traditional community services background is not essential if you can demonstrate effective leadership and accountable service delivery.
  
This may also suit an experienced Coordinator or senior leader from a larger organisation who is ready to step into broader management responsibility.
  
Why Central Highlands Regional Council?
  
This is your opportunity to influence more than day-to-day operations: shape a diverse portfolio and the way services evolve across the region.
  
Council is progressing initiatives across libraries, arts, youth, heritage, events and community grants. You will build on this work, strengthen your team and improve the experience of the communities Council serves.
You will have room to introduce fresh ideas while working within a supportive and accountable local government environment.
  
For a leader motivated by variety, problem-solving and community impact, this is an opportunity to make the role your own.
  
The opportunity offers:
  • $210,000–$252,000 Total Remuneration Package
  • A visible senior leadership role across a broad and varied portfolio
  • Relocation assistance for candidates moving to the region
  • Potential access to Council accommodation
Based in Emerald, you can enjoy the benefits of regional living, a welcoming community and access to the Central Highlands’ remarkable natural attractions.
If you are ready to develop people, improve services and contribute to the future of the Central Highlands, we would welcome a confidential discussion.
  
Be part of something that matters, with like-minded people who truly care. One Place. Many Paths. Choose Yours Here.
  
Apply Now
  
To apply, please submit your CV and cover letter via the 'Apply Now' button or contact:
  
Adrian Holder
Lead Search & Select Consultant
Public Sector People
M: 0410 510 431
E: adrian@publicsectorpeople.com.au
  
Applications close Tuesday 3rd November at 5pm

job.title: Facilities Manager
job.description:
About the Organisation
PSP is supporting a purpose-driven organisation providing housing solutions that support people and communities across Australia. With a focus on delivering quality housing and positive resident outcomes, the organisation manages a diverse portfolio spanning social housing, affordable housing and Specialist Disability Accommodation (SDA).

This is an opportunity to join an organisation where property and facilities management plays an important role in ensuring residents have access to safe, functional and well-maintained homes. Working collaboratively with a broader Property Services team, you will contribute to the ongoing performance of a significant residential asset and help establish strong operational foundations from the outset.

About the Role
The Facilities Manager is responsible for the day-to-day operation, maintenance and presentation of a high-profile, 27-storey mixed-use residential building in Perth CBD, comprising 219 apartments across social housing, affordable housing and SDA.

Reporting to the Manager, Corporate Assets, you will take ownership of onsite facilities operations, working closely with the wider WA Property Services team to coordinate maintenance, manage contractors and ensure building services and infrastructure operate safely, efficiently and in line with relevant compliance requirements.

With the building preparing to open, this is an opportunity to be involved from the early stages, commencing approximately six weeks before opening to help establish maintenance processes, coordinate contractors and ensure the building is operationally ready.

The role offers a broad mix of responsibilities across building infrastructure, preventative and responsive maintenance, defect management, inspections and upgrades. You will oversee contractor performance across essential services, monitor compliance, maintain asset and maintenance records, manage operating expenditure and respond to issues as they arise.

You will also work closely with Housing Officers and the Allocations team to coordinate repairs and maintenance across individual dwellings, including vacate inspections, while helping maintain a positive experience for residents.

This is a hands on, site-based opportunity for someone who enjoys taking ownership, solving practical problems and ensuring a building is maintained to a high standard. You will have the autonomy to manage day-to-day operations while working collaboratively with an established property team.

About You
You are an experienced facilities or property professional with a strong understanding of building infrastructure, maintenance and contractor management. You enjoy being close to the operational side of a building and are confident coordinating competing priorities in a live residential environment.

You bring experience managing preventative and reactive maintenance, overseeing contractors and service providers, identifying defects and ensuring issues are followed through to resolution. You understand the importance of building compliance, workplace health and safety and maintaining accurate asset and maintenance records.

You will be organised, proactive and comfortable working autonomously, with the communication skills to build effective relationships with contractors, internal stakeholders and residents. You can manage day-to-day operational challenges while maintaining a strong focus on safety, service delivery and building presentation.

Residential apartment or mixed use building experience will be highly regarded, as will exposure to social housing, affordable housing, SDA or other residential environments supporting people with diverse needs. 

This role would strongly suit:
  • A Facilities Manager with experience managing high-density residential apartment buildings or mixed-use developments.
  • A residential property or facilities professional experienced in contractor coordination, building maintenance and defect management.
  • A building operations professional with a strong understanding of essential services, compliance and preventative maintenance.
  • A facilities or property professional from a community housing, affordable housing, SDA or other residential environment looking to take ownership of a significant building.
Relevant qualifications in facilities management, building services, property, engineering, a trade or a related discipline are desirable. A current driver's licence is required, along with the ability to complete relevant employment screening checks.

The Opportunity
This is an opportunity to take ownership of facilities operations within a significant residential building, playing a key role in preparing the asset for opening and establishing effective day-to-day maintenance and contractor management processes.

You will join a collaborative property team and contribute to maintaining a safe, functional and welcoming environment for residents across a diverse mixed tenure housing model.

After-hours work is expected to be minimal and will be remunerated in accordance with the applicable arrangements.

Location: Perth CBD.

Application Process
For a confidential discussion or to receive further information about the opportunity, please contact Sarah Kettlewell 03 8535 3111 at Public Sector People.

Engineer Strategy – Water & Wastewater

Public Sector People is partnering with Mackay Regional Council to appoint an Engineer Strategy – Water & Wastewater within its Infrastructure Planning team.

This is an excellent opportunity for a Civil, Water or Environmental Engineer looking to move beyond traditional design and delivery into a role where their technical expertise will directly influence future infrastructure investment, network performance and regional growth.

With a growing population and continued investment in essential infrastructure, Mackay offers the opportunity to work on meaningful engineering challenges while enjoying the lifestyle benefits of coastal Queensland.

The Opportunity Reporting to the Coordinator Strategy – Water & Wastewater, you will contribute to the long-term planning and development of the region's essential water and sewerage networks.

Combining technical engineering, data analysis and strategic planning, you will help Council identify future infrastructure requirements, assess network capacity and develop practical solutions to support sustainable growth.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Undertaking hydraulic modelling and network capacity assessments to support future infrastructure planning.
  • Contributing to water and wastewater infrastructure strategies, asset management plans and capital works programs.
  • Preparing concept designs, feasibility assessments, business cases and technical reports.
  • Providing engineering advice on development applications and proposed infrastructure connections.
  • Analysing network performance, asset condition and future demand to inform investment priorities.
  • Working with internal teams, developers and external consultants to deliver effective infrastructure solutions.
About You We are seeking an engineer who enjoys solving technical problems, working collaboratively and contributing to longer-term infrastructure outcomes.

You will ideally bring:
  • Tertiary qualifications in Civil, Environmental or a related Engineering discipline.
  • Experience in water and/or wastewater engineering, infrastructure planning, design or asset management.
  • An understanding of hydraulic modelling, network planning and infrastructure capacity assessments.
  • The ability to interpret engineering data and develop practical, evidence-based recommendations.
  • Strong communication, technical reporting and stakeholder engagement skills.
Experience within local government, water utilities or engineering consulting will be highly regarded.

Importantly, you do not need to have spent your entire career in strategic planning. Engineers with a strong technical foundation in water and wastewater infrastructure who are looking to develop their strategic planning expertise are encouraged to apply.

Why Mackay Regional Council?

Mackay Regional Council provides essential infrastructure and services to a growing regional community of more than 125,000 residents.
This opportunity offers:
  • Career development: Broaden your engineering experience across network strategy, infrastructure planning and asset management.
  • Meaningful projects: Help shape long-term capital investment decisions that will support the region for decades.
  • Technical variety: Gain exposure to hydraulic modelling, development assessment, infrastructure forecasting and strategic projects.
  • Supportive environment: Join an established Infrastructure Planning team and collaborate with experienced technical professionals.
  • Competitive remuneration: Permanent opportunity with a base salary of $115,000–$122,000 plus superannuation.
  • Relocation assistance: Available for the successful candidate.
Discover the Mackay Lifestyle Located on Queensland's tropical coast, Mackay offers an attractive balance of career opportunity and lifestyle.

With beautiful beaches, access to the Whitsundays, affordable housing options and a welcoming regional community, Mackay is an excellent place to build both your career and your future.

Apply Now

job.description:
Implementation Lead Strategy, Water & Wastewater
Mackay Regional Council | Level 8.1–8.5 ($135,861 to $156,754) | 36.25 Hours per Week | Relocation Assistance

Public Sector People are partnering with Mackay Regional Council to appoint an Implementation Lead Strategy, Water & Wastewater — a key technical role turning strategic infrastructure priorities into coordinated programmes of work.

This is an opportunity to take ownership of major water and wastewater projects, progressing business cases, scoping and approvals so infrastructure is ready to support the region’s future growth. Bring your project expertise to meaningful work while enjoying the balance of a 36.25-hour working week.

The Role
Working within Council’s Infrastructure Planning Program, you will help move established project concepts into implementation, coordinating internal teams, consultants and contractors. Key priorities include:
  • Major sewer redirection infrastructure between the northern and southern treatment catchments
  • Renewal of the main raw water pipeline between the pump station and water treatment plant
  • Water treatment plant upgrades and other major water infrastructure projects
  • Business case development, project scoping and investment prioritisation
  • Planning, design coordination, approvals and preparation for delivery
This is a technical project lead position with no direct reports. Your impact will come through sound judgement, initiative and the ability to bring stakeholders together to move complex projects forward.

You will work closely with experienced water and wastewater professionals, with access to support and guidance as you build your understanding of Mackay’s infrastructure needs.

You will also:
  • Translate adopted strategies into structured programmes with clear milestones and outcomes
  • Coordinate multidisciplinary inputs and manage consultant and contractor interfaces
  • Develop business cases, financial analysis and investment recommendations
  • Engage regulators, government agencies and funding bodies to support approvals and funding
  • Monitor environmental, regulatory and financial risks and programme dependencies
  • Provide clear reporting and advice on progress, risks and strategic alignment
Council is seeking someone who can understand the bigger picture, work through the detail and take responsibility for progressing the work.

About You
You are a self-motivated water and wastewater professional with strong project experience and the confidence to turn plans into practical outcomes.

You can communicate effectively with technical specialists, consultants and contractors, build productive relationships and explain complex issues clearly.

Experience in councils, utilities, consultancies, government or the private sector is welcome.

You will bring:
  • Relevant engineering or project management qualifications. Extensive comparable experience in major water projects may also be considered
  • At least five years’ relevant experience in water and wastewater planning, strategy implementation or programme delivery
  • Significant experience coordinating complex multidisciplinary initiatives and external consultants or contractors
  • Strong capability in business cases, prioritisation, investment planning and financial analysis
  • Knowledge of water and wastewater infrastructure, regulatory requirements, asset planning and capital delivery
  • Experience engaging regulators, government agencies and funding bodies, supported by strong reporting and communication skills
  • A General Construction Induction White Card and Queensland C-class driver licence, or interstate equivalent transferable within three months
  
Civil, mechanical and other relevant engineering backgrounds with substantial water-sector experience will be considered. RPEQ registration and hydraulic modelling experience, including WaterGEMS or InfoWorks CS, are desirable rather than essential.

Why Join Mackay Regional Council?
Join an experienced infrastructure team working on major projects that will shape water and wastewater services for years to come. This role offers the scope to apply your technical strengths, grow your project responsibility and see your work make a lasting regional contribution.

This role offers:
  • Level 8.1–8.5 remuneration, with appointment based on experience
  • A 36.25-hour working week and a strong focus on work-life balance
  • Scope to discuss flexible working arrangements, including an RDO request
  • Relocation assistance to support your move to Mackay
  • Potential for hybrid work once you are established and understand regional requirements, subject to agreement
  • Support from experienced colleagues and exposure to major strategic infrastructure projects
  
Mackay offers a coastal lifestyle, a strong community and the opportunity to combine rewarding infrastructure work with more time to enjoy life outside work.

job.title: Manager Water & Wastewater
job.description:
Manager Water & Wastewater
Isaac Regional Council | Isaac Region QLD | Operational Leadership | Circa $230k to $250 TRP
  
Public Sector People are proud to partner with Isaac Regional Council to recruit a Manager Water & Wastewater—a key leadership opportunity responsible for safe, reliable and compliant water, wastewater and recycled water services across the region.
  
Reporting to the Director Infrastructure Services, you will lead a broad operational portfolio encompassing treatment plants, networks, pump stations, bulk water storage and dam safety, laboratory services and SCADA. Your focus will be on supporting the people who deliver these essential services while strengthening operational performance and regulatory compliance.
  
Council is seeking an experienced water industry leader who can build confidence within the team, develop its supervisory capability and provide practical direction through change. Strong treatment knowledge is particularly valuable, alongside the ability to oversee network operations and balance safety, customer service and financial outcomes.
  
The Role
  
This is an opportunity to shape how essential services are delivered and build leadership capability throughout the team. Early priorities include strengthening team cohesion, coaching coordinators and supervisors, improving processes and addressing technical challenges, particularly within treatment operations.
  
Working closely with the Director and other infrastructure managers, you will drive service improvements, support strategic and operational asset management and contribute to Council’s future commercialised water and waste business unit.
  
Key responsibilities include:
  • Leading, coaching and developing water and wastewater teams, building capability, accountability and succession
  • Overseeing treatment, reticulation, pumping and bulk distribution services across a geographically distributed customer base
  • Maintaining drinking water quality, wastewater and recycled water environmental compliance and associated reporting
  • Improving operations and maintenance systems, asset performance and service reliability
  • Managing operational resources, monitoring financial performance and identifying efficiency opportunities
  • Overseeing bulk water storage and dam safety, asset inspections, audits and corrective actions
  • Maintaining emergency preparedness, including responsibilities under the Theresa Creek Dam Emergency Action Plan
  • Building trusted relationships with regulators, customers, unions, government agencies and elected representatives
  • Supporting organisational change and developing a positive, integrated and safety-focused team culture
  
About You
  
You are an experienced water and wastewater operations leader who combines technical judgement with proven people management. You enjoy developing others, resolving operational challenges and building systems that enable teams to deliver consistently.
  
You will bring:
  • At least five years’ experience at local government management level or in a comparable role
  • Experience managing operations and maintenance across water and wastewater treatment, pump stations and networks
  • Strong people leadership, coaching and change management capability
  • Sound knowledge of water industry reporting, regulatory obligations and Australian industry practice
  • Experience leading operational and maintenance service improvements
  • Strong financial, resource management and problem-solving skills
  • Excellent communication and negotiation skills, with the judgement to work effectively in a public sector environment
  • Experience engaging customers, unions, regulators and other stakeholders
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, a Construction White Card and a valid driver licence
  
Tertiary qualifications in engineering, science, environmental management or a related discipline are desirable. Eligibility for CPEng or RPEQ, and postgraduate qualifications in business, asset, maintenance or operations management, are highly regarded but not mandatory.
  
Local government experience will be an advantage, but Council also welcomes experienced leaders from utilities and other water industry organisations who bring strong operational expertise, people leadership and an understanding of community service obligations.
  
Why Join Isaac Regional Council
  
Isaac is a region that feeds, powers and builds communities. This role offers the chance to make a direct contribution to the reliability of essential services while developing the people who support the region’s long-term future.
  
  • Base salary of $170,000–$190,000, with flexibility considered for an exceptional candidate
  • Council housing and vehicle arrangements, or allowances in lieu, subject to agreed terms
  • Relocation assistance to support your move to the region
  • A broad leadership portfolio covering water, wastewater and recycled water services
  • The opportunity to strengthen team capability, improve operations and influence future service delivery
  
Council’s preference is for the successful candidate to be based within the Isaac region, providing visible leadership and becoming part of the communities they serve. The role includes responding to operational escalations and supporting emergency readiness when required.

job.title: Manager City Strategy
job.description:
About Melton City Council

Melton City Council serves a rapidly growing municipality in Melbourne’s west, where expanding communities, new employment precincts and major infrastructure investment are shaping the city’s future.

Strategic planning plays a central role in managing this growth. Council is planning for new development while responding to the needs of established communities, ensuring land use, infrastructure and community facilities support the municipality’s long-term future.

Council is seeking a Manager City Strategy to provide strategic direction and engaged leadership across a diverse portfolio. This is an opportunity to influence how Melton develops, lead a capable team and build the relationships needed to translate strategy into practical outcomes.

About the Role

The Manager City Strategy leads Council’s strategic planning, urban design and heritage, open space and community infrastructure planning, sustainability and climate resilience functions.

Strategic planning is a key priority, with a significant program of work across growth areas, emerging industrial and employment land, planning scheme amendments and major government projects. You will guide the preparation of policies and planning frameworks that establish a clear direction for future land use and development.

Current priorities include the Melton East Precinct Structure Plan and engagement with State Government projects. You will ensure Council’s interests are clearly represented and that planning advice reflects the connections between growth, infrastructure, employment and community needs.

The broader portfolio brings together functions that influence the quality and sustainability of the municipality. Urban design and heritage inform how places develop and retain their identity, while open space and community infrastructure planning help establish what growing and established communities will need into the future.

The department also develops policy and strategic direction across sustainability, climate resilience and circular economy. You will ensure these priorities are considered alongside land use and infrastructure planning, with clear frameworks that other parts of Council can use to guide their work.

A central part of the role will be bringing clarity and coordination to the department’s work program. Supported by coordinators and specialist staff, you will establish priorities, clarify responsibilities and ensure the team has the direction and support needed to deliver.

You will work closely with colleagues across Council to connect strategic planning with implementation. This requires early engagement, an understanding of operational needs and a collaborative approach to developing policies and frameworks that can be put into practice.

Beyond the organisation, you will build productive relationships with government agencies, developers, industry and community stakeholders. You will represent Council confidently, provide clear advice and help progress complex matters involving different interests and responsibilities.
  
  
About You

You bring substantial experience in strategic planning, land use or a closely related field, together with the leadership capability to guide a multidisciplinary team.

You understand the planning challenges and opportunities associated with a growing municipality. You can provide sound direction across growth area planning, planning scheme amendments and emerging land use priorities, while considering the infrastructure, environmental and community implications of those decisions.

You are an engaging and collaborative leader who takes an active interest in the team’s work. You provide clear expectations, practical guidance and the support people need to contribute confidently and take ownership of outcomes.

You can bring clarity to a broad portfolio, helping coordinators and specialists understand priorities, manage competing demands and work effectively together. You value their expertise while maintaining accountability for performance and delivery.

You build strong relationships across an organisation and understand that effective strategy depends on the involvement of the people who will implement it. You listen to different perspectives, work constructively through issues and help colleagues reach decisions that move work forward.

You are also comfortable representing Council externally, engaging with industry and government, and communicating complex planning matters clearly. You combine strategic thinking with a practical approach to getting things done.

Local government experience would be valuable, although Council is open to candidates from other relevant environments who bring strong planning expertise, effective leadership and a clear understanding of the public outcomes this work supports.

Most importantly, you will bring energy, sound judgement and a collaborative approach to leading the team and shaping Melton’s future.

Application Process

Public Sector People is partnering with Melton City Council to recruit this important leadership position.

For a confidential discussion or to request a copy of the position description, please contact Blanche Grimaux at Public Sector People.

To apply, please submit your CV and a brief cover letter via the link.

job.title: Municipal Building Surveyor
job.description:
About Melton City Council

Melton City Council is one of Australia’s fastest-growing municipalities, with expanding communities, new development and emerging employment precincts shaping its future.

This growth creates a significant opportunity for Council’s building services function. As the municipality evolves, the service needs the leadership, capability and systems to respond to increasing demand while protecting community safety and delivering its statutory responsibilities.

Council is seeking a Municipal Building Surveyor who wants to help shape that future. This appointment offers genuine scope to influence how the department is structured, how its people are supported and how building services are delivered across the municipality.

With senior management seeking a clearer direction for the function, and work already underway to address outstanding compliance matters, the incoming MBS will have a strong platform from which to build the next phase of the service.

About the Role

The Municipal Building Surveyor is responsible for administering Council’s statutory building functions and providing leadership, technical oversight and direction to the building services team.

Alongside these statutory responsibilities, the role offers an opportunity to shape the department’s ongoing structure and operating model. Working with senior management, you will assess the service’s needs, clarify responsibilities and identify the leadership arrangements and technical capability required to support a growing municipality.

The service’s current focus is on compliance, enforcement, inspections and Council’s broader municipal building responsibilities. Council does not currently issue building permits, with the incoming MBS expected to review the service model and provide considered advice on its future scope, including whether a municipal permit offering would be appropriate.

A key priority will be establishing a clear understanding of the team’s workload, capability and outstanding matters, then ensuring work is prioritised and delivered consistently. You will support staff to make sound decisions, provide clear technical guidance and strengthen accountability across the service.

Swimming pool and spa compliance work is also underway, with an established team progressing Council’s obligations in this area. There is scope to move the department towards a more planned and proactive approach, with clearer priorities, stronger reporting and a shared understanding of what effective service delivery looks like.

You will help translate that direction into practical changes to team structure, processes and day-to-day operations. You will also provide clear advice on complex or sensitive building matters, ensuring statutory decisions are well considered and that senior leaders understand the service’s risks, priorities and resource requirements.

About You

You are an experienced building surveyor with Unlimited registration in Victoria and the technical capability required to perform the statutory responsibilities of a Municipal Building Surveyor.

You bring strong knowledge of building legislation, compliance, enforcement and regulatory decision-making, supported by experience managing complex building matters.

You are motivated by the opportunity to build and shape a department. You can assess how a service is operating, identify the capability and structure it needs, and work with senior management and staff to turn that thinking into practical improvements.

You are a visible and engaged leader who provides clear direction, supports staff and follows through on priorities. You establish expectations while giving your team the guidance and confidence to take ownership of their work.

You are comfortable leading through change and reviewing established practices with an open mind. You will take the time to understand the team’s strengths and challenges, then set a clear direction that supports both immediate delivery and the department’s longer-term development.

Experience in local government would be valuable, alongside the ability to work collaboratively with senior leaders and provide sound advice in a municipal regulatory environment.

Most importantly, you will bring energy, sound judgement and a constructive leadership style, with the ambition to shape a capable building service that keeps pace with the Melton community.

Application Process

Public Sector People is partnering with Melton City Council to recruit this important statutory leadership position.

For a confidential discussion or to request a copy of the position description, please contact Blanche Grimaux at Public Sector People.

To apply, please submit your CV and a brief cover letter via the link. Applications close on Monday 2nd November 2026.
