job.title: People & Culture Business Partner
job.description:
About Frankston City Council
Frankston City Council is an active local government organisation serving a diverse and growing community across Melbourne’s south-east. Council is committed to delivering high quality services and creating a positive experience for its employees, residents and broader community.

The People & Culture team plays an important role in supporting Council’s leaders to build capable, engaged and high-performing teams. With a focus on trusted partnerships, practical advice and continuous improvement, the team works across Council to support the full employee lifecycle and deliver people outcomes aligned to Council’s priorities.


About the Role
The People & Culture Business Partner is a key role within Frankston City Council’s People & Culture team, partnering with leaders across Council to provide strategic and operational HR advice across the full employee lifecycle.

Reporting to the Coordinator Business Partnering, you will work closely with Managers, Directors and people leaders across Council to provide practical, contemporary HR advice across employee relations, performance management, organisational change, workforce planning, employment matters and the interpretation of Council’s Enterprise Agreement and relevant legislation.

This is a genuine HR generalist Business Partner role, with a strong focus on employee relations. You will manage and advise on a range of complex people matters, including performance management, grievances, workplace disputes, misconduct and complaints relating to discrimination, harassment and bullying.

You will be trusted to lead investigations and provide sound advice to leaders, ensuring matters are managed effectively, fairly and in line with Council’s policies, legislation and employment framework.

You will also support organisational change and consultation processes, contribute to People & Culture projects and initiatives, and use people data and insights to inform decision making and workforce planning. The role provides the opportunity to work across a broad range of HR matters rather than being limited to one specialist area.

You will join a collaborative Business Partnering team, within a broader People & Culture function of approximately 20 professionals. Council is looking for someone who is proactive, energetic and willing to roll up their sleeves and contribute wherever needed.


About You
An experienced HR professional with strong generalist HR capability and a proven ability to partner with leaders and provide practical, strategic advice across the employee lifecycle.

Strong employee relations experience will be important, particularly across performance management, workplace investigations and complex employee matters. The ability to confidently interpret employment legislation, Enterprise Agreements, policies and procedures, and translate these into clear, practical advice for leaders.

Strong stakeholder management skills are equally important. This role will suit someone who enjoys working closely with leaders at all levels, influencing outcomes and building trusted partnerships, while also having the confidence to challenge, advise and provide an alternative perspective when required.

A proactive and solutions focused approach, together with the ability to work autonomously and manage competing priorities, will be essential. This is a broad HR role within a fast moving environment, respond confidently to a range of people matters and step in to support the broader team when needed.

Experience within a large, complex or fast paced organisation will be highly regarded. Previous Local Government experience is desirable, however Council is open to strong HR Business Partners from other large, unionised environments who can demonstrate relevant transferable experience.
  
This role would strongly suit:
  • An experienced HR Business Partner with strong generalist HR and employee relations experience
  • A People & Culture professional looking to step into a genuine partnering role with broad exposure across the employee lifecycle
  • A Business Partner or experienced Advisor who enjoys working closely with leaders, providing practical advice and helping resolve complex people matters
  • An experienced HR professional from Local Government, health, education, NFP or another large unionised organisation looking to bring their skills into a diverse Council environment
A relevant qualification in Human Resources or a related discipline is desirable, together with demonstrated ER experience, strong knowledge of employment law and contemporary HR practices. Experience working within a large, complex or fast-paced organisation will be highly regarded.


The Opportunity
This is an opportunity to join Frankston City Council at an exciting time and contribute to a growing People & Culture function.

This role will have the opportunity to build strong relationships across Council and provide meaningful support to leaders as the organisation continues to evolve.

You will join an experienced and collaborative P&C team where your HR expertise, proactive approach and ability to build trusted relationships will be valued.

Frankston City Council also offers a range of benefits designed to support flexibility, wellbeing and work life balance, including:
  • Additional paid leave between the Christmas and New Year period, on top of four weeks annual leave
  • Monthly RDO arrangements
  • Hybrid and flexible working arrangements
  • Purchased leave
  • Paid Parental Leave
  • Free onsite parking at the Civic Centre
  • Salary sacrifice gym membership at Peninsula Aquatic Recreation Centre
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
  • Social Club and employee activities
  • Professional and career development opportunities
Salary: Band 6, $100,338 + superannuation

Application Process
For a confidential discussion or to receive a copy of the position description, please contact Sarah Kettlewell on 0478 041 199 or sarah@publicsectorpeople.com.au

Public Sector People are partnering exclusively with Frankston City Council on this appointment. All applications and enquiries will be managed by Public Sector People.

job.title: Manager Engineering Services
job.description:
Manager Engineering Services
Isaac Regional Council | Isaac Region QLD | Infrastructure Leadership | Circa $230k to $250 TRP
  
Public Sector People are proud to partner with Isaac Regional Council to recruit a Manager Engineering Services—an expanded leadership opportunity bringing together infrastructure planning, capital delivery and technical services across a diverse regional portfolio.
  
You will lead and develop the people who plan, design and support the delivery of infrastructure for Isaac’s communities. With the team’s scope recently expanded, this is an opportunity to establish clear priorities, strengthen capability and shape how the function works within Council’s Infrastructure Services Directorate.
  
Council is seeking a leader who combines technical credibility with the ability to motivate people, negotiate competing priorities and turn plans into practical outcomes. Your influence will extend across transport, water and wastewater projects, asset renewals, road access and infrastructure agreements with industry.
  
The Role
  
You will oversee infrastructure planning, design coordination and capital delivery, working closely with other managers and asset owners to develop balanced investment programs that respond to community needs and Council priorities.
  
An early focus will be bringing the expanded team together, clarifying responsibilities and supporting recruitment and development in key positions while maintaining momentum across the capital program. Most detailed design is outsourced, so your ability to scope requirements, manage consultants and assess technical quality will be central to success.
  
Key responsibilities include:
  • Leading, coaching and developing engineering and technical staff, building a collaborative and performance-focused culture
  • Developing 5-, 10- and 20-year infrastructure priorities and capital works programs across Council portfolios
  • Coordinating infrastructure planning, asset renewals and delivery of transport and water-related capital projects
  • Managing external design consultants, technical specifications, construction standards and engineering reports
  • Overseeing heavy vehicle access approvals, third-party road corridor access and infrastructure agreements with mining companies and developers
  • Providing engineering input into development and operational works assessments in collaboration with Council’s planning teams
  • Coordinating bridge inspection requirements and oversight of Council aerodromes and aircraft landing areas
  • Identifying grant opportunities and preparing funding submissions for infrastructure investment
  • Building trusted relationships with government agencies, industry, contractors, elected representatives and communities
  
About You
  
You are an experienced civil infrastructure leader who can provide direction to a broad team, develop emerging talent and balance engineering requirements with commercial, community and political considerations. You bring sound judgement, a pragmatic approach and the confidence to negotiate constructively with industry and government stakeholders.
  
You will bring:
  • Proven people leadership, with experience managing department functions, coaching staff and building capability
  • At least 10 years’ demonstrated civil engineering experience, or significant other relevant experience
  • Strong infrastructure planning, asset management and capital program development capability
  • Experience leading design and technical services across roads, drainage, traffic or related infrastructure
  • The ability to manage consultants and contractors, interpret technical designs and deliver value for money
  • Knowledge of civil construction and maintenance, relevant Queensland requirements and TMR specifications
  • Strong communication, negotiation and stakeholder engagement skills, including managing competing priorities
  • Proficiency in Microsoft applications, including Microsoft Project
  • A Construction White Card and valid driver licence
  
A Civil Engineering degree, or a similar engineering degree with relevant civil experience, is desirable. RPEQ certification and postgraduate management qualifications are also highly regarded.
  
Local government experience will be an advantage, particularly where you understand capital planning, approvals and public sector decision-making. Council also welcomes leaders from consulting, infrastructure and other relevant sectors who can demonstrate strong people leadership and adapt to the local government environment. Specialist aviation experience is not a prerequisite; the role is supported by staff with operational aerodrome expertise.
  
Why Join Isaac Regional Council
  
Isaac is a region that feeds, powers and builds communities. This role offers the opportunity to connect significant infrastructure investment with the everyday needs of regional communities, while working with industry and government on the infrastructure that supports the region’s future.
  
  • Base salary of $170,000–$190,000, with flexibility considered for an exceptional candidate
  • Council housing and vehicle arrangements, or allowances in lieu, subject to agreed terms
  • Relocation assistance to support your move to the region
  • An expanded leadership remit with influence over infrastructure planning and capital delivery
  • The opportunity to develop your team, shape ways of working and make a visible contribution to community services
Council’s preference is for the successful candidate to be based within the Isaac region, providing visible leadership and becoming part of the communities they serve.
  
Apply Now
  
To apply, please submit your CV and cover letter via the Apply Now button or contact:
  
Adrian Holder
Lead Search & Select Consultant
Public Sector People
E: adrian@publicsectorpeople.com.au
  
Applications close: 5th November at 5pm
  
Applications will be reviewed and interviews may be conducted throughout the campaign. Council reserves the right to close the process early if a suitable candidate is appointed. Early applications are encouraged.

job.title: Automation Technician
job.description:
Industrial Automation Technologist / Technician

Location: Wetherill Park, Sydney
Industry: Advanced Manufacturing (Injection Moulding & Automation) Employment Type: Full-time, 24/7 manufacturing environment

About the Role
Our client, an established manufacturing operation based in Wetherill Park, is seeking an experienced Industrial Automation Technologist/Technician to join their team. This is a hands-on, technically diverse role supporting PLC-driven automation, industrial robotics, injection moulding machinery, and high-speed production equipment across a 24/7 site.

You'll be a key technical point of contact for production issues relating to equipment performance, product quality, and efficiency — working closely with Production, Maintenance, and Quality teams to minimise downtime and maximise OEE.
This role blends fault-finding, preventative maintenance, die setting, process optimisation, and continuous improvement, with genuine exposure to automation upgrades and manufacturing improvement projects.

Key Responsibilities
Automation & Technical Maintenance
  • Troubleshoot and maintain industrial automation and production equipment across a 24/7 environment
  • Service, repair, and set up injection moulding machines, industrial robots, IML systems, and auxiliary equipment
  • Fault-find and replace mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, and pneumatic components
  • Integrate industrial robots into material handling, inspection, and packaging applications, including safety interlock verification
  • Perform preventative and predictive maintenance, equipment upgrades, and calibrations
  • Complete major equipment overhauls and support complex machine, processing, and die-setting issues
Production & Process Support
  • Act as a key technical contact for production issues affecting output, quality, reliability, and efficiency
  • Perform die, insert, and colour changes, including machine start-ups and shutdowns
  • Set, adjust, and optimise robotics, machine software, and production process parameters
  • Troubleshoot production faults, including IML and high-speed packaging equipment
  • Maintain target cycle times while ensuring finished products meet specification
Continuous Improvement & Problem Solving
  • Investigate recurring and new faults using structured root-cause analysis; implement corrective and preventative actions
  • Analyse downtime, rejects, defects, and waste to identify improvement opportunities
  • Support automation design, programming, commissioning, and equipment upgrades
  • Maintain accurate records of downtime, rejects, NCRs, maintenance activities, and corrective actions
Quality & Compliance
  • Work closely with Quality Assurance to ensure equipment and processes meet product, customer, and regulatory requirements
  • Ensure compliance with site quality systems, HACCP, and applicable food safety requirements
  • Verify new or modified automation systems before production handover
Safety & Team Support
  • Work in line with WHS legislation, site safety procedures, and permit requirements
  • Identify, report, and rectify hazards and near misses
  • Coordinate with third-party service technicians when required
  • Support training and technical upskilling of production and maintenance personnel
  • Communicate and escalate technical issues across shifts to maintain operational continuity
About You
  • Proven experience in industrial automation, robotics, and/or injection moulding within a manufacturing environment
  • Strong mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, and pneumatic fault-finding skills
  • Experience with PLC-driven systems and industrial robot integration
  • Die-setting experience highly regarded
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced, 24/7 production environment
  • Strong root-cause analysis and continuous improvement mindset
  • Food safety/HACCP exposure an advantage
  • Ability to train and support colleagues, and communicate effectively across shifts
Why Apply
  • Stable, full-time opportunity with genuine exposure to modern automation technology
  • Hands-on role combining automation, robotics, and process engineering — not a narrow, single-skill position
  • Real input into equipment upgrades and manufacturing improvement projects
  • Work within an established, well-resourced manufacturing operation

Experienced Archicad User Ready for a Career Pivot: You may be a Senior Drafter, BIM Coordinator, Archicad specialist or highly experienced residential drafting professional who loves helping others and wants to move away from day-to-day drafting into a training-focused career.
Ideally, you'll bring:

  • Strong interpersonal and presentation skills

Why Consider This Opportunity?
This is a unique opportunity to take your technical Archicad knowledge and turn it into a long-term career in training and capability development.
You'll join a major Australian building organisation, work closely with BIM and L&D specialists, gain exposure to drafting teams nationally and have the opportunity to become a recognised technical training specialist within the business.

job.title: Information Access Manager
job.description:
Location: Sydney, NSW
Salary: $178,021 to $203,376 + 12% Super
Work Type: Full Time, Permanent
Public Sector People on behalf of City of Sydney

Lead the City's information access function and become the trusted expert driving transparency, sound decision making and best practice governance across one of Australia's most progressive councils.

Public Sector People are proud to partner with the City of Sydney to recruit an Information Access Manager within the Digital and Information Services Unit.

This is a unique opportunity for an experienced GIPA or Freedom of Information professional to lead the City's information access function as its delegated decision-maker under the Government Information (Public Access) Act 2009. Leading a specialist team, you'll make complex statutory decisions, provide trusted advice to the Executive Leadership Team and work across every area of the organisation to ensure the City continues to uphold the principles of transparency, accountability and open government.

This is a role for someone who enjoys applying legislation to complex situations, can confidently make independent decisions and has the judgement to navigate sensitive matters with professionalism, diplomacy and integrity.

About the Role

Reporting to the Manager Information Services, you will be responsible for:
  • Lead and develop the City's specialist Information Access team.
  • Act as the City's delegated decision-maker under the GIPA Act.
  • Assess and determine complex GIPA applications, subpoenas and other information access matters.
  • Provide expert advice to Directors, Executives and business units on information access legislation and disclosure obligations.
  • Represent the City in reviews with the Information and Privacy Commission and NSW Civil and Administrative Tribunal (NCAT).
  • Drive proactive release initiatives and promote a culture of open government across the organisation.
  • Develop policies, procedures and education programs that strengthen legislative compliance and organisational capability.
  • Work collaboratively with Legal, Governance, Archives and operational teams to resolve complex information access matters.
 
 
What You'll Bring
  • Extensive experience administering the Government Information (Public Access) Act (GIPA) or equivalent Freedom of Information legislation.
  • Demonstrated experience making independent statutory decisions within a complex public sector environment.
  • Strong understanding of balancing transparency with public interest considerations and legislative obligations.
  • Experience advising senior executives and confidently influencing stakeholders on sensitive matters.
  • Leadership experience managing and developing high-performing specialist teams.
  • Excellent judgement, resilience and communication skills, with the confidence to make, explain and defend complex decisions.
  • Tertiary qualifications in Information Management, Governance or a related discipline, or equivalent experience.


Why City of Sydney?
  • Lead the City's information access function as the delegated decision-maker under the GIPA Act.
  • Make decisions that directly influence transparency, governance and public trust.
  • Work closely with senior executives, Legal and Governance on complex and high-profile matters.
  • Join one of Australia's leading local government organisations, committed to innovation, collaboration and continuous improvement.
  
Ready to become the trusted authority on information access at the City of Sydney?

Contact Esme Lynch at Public Sector People on 0413 282 765 or email esme@publicsectorpeople.com.au for a confidential discussion.

Applications close: 11:59pm, Thursday 15th October 2026.

  • Demonstrated experience producing solution designs, technical roadmaps and architecture documentation.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills with the ability to engage both technical and non-technical audiences.

job.title: Project Manager (Housing)

A new building is only part of the picture. Making it ready for people to call home takes coordinated planning, clear decisions and strong operational leadership.
 
Public Sector People is seeking a Project Manager for a purpose-led organisation delivering social and affordable housing across Greater Brisbane and surrounding areas.
 
This role will bring new housing developments, acquisitions and service expansions into operation, ensuring properties, teams, systems and services are ready before residents move in.
 
Based in Brisbane, with travel to development and property sites, you will lead a team of two and work across the organisation to coordinate delivery, resolve challenges and oversee the transition into stable day-to-day operations.
 
The opportunity
 
You will take ownership of the operational readiness program, translating development commitments into practical plans with clear milestones, responsibilities and measures of success.
 
Your responsibilities will include:
  • Leading readiness plans across multiple projects, managing timelines, budgets, resources, risks and dependencies.
  • Coordinating property handovers, including asset information, defects, compliance documentation, utilities and contractor mobilisation.
  • Bringing together tenant allocations, sign-ups, move-ins and customer communications to support a coordinated occupancy process.
  • Ensuring systems, data, procedures, staffing and training are prepared and tested before opening.
  • Leading cross-functional working groups and working with developers, builders, government agencies, contractors and service partners.
  • Providing executive reporting and recommendations on readiness, emerging risks and decisions required.
  • Supporting early operations and transferring outstanding actions and ongoing responsibilities to the relevant teams.
About you
 
You will bring substantial experience delivering complex projects, operational mobilisation, service transitions or major change initiatives involving multiple teams and stakeholders.
 
You can turn competing requirements into a clear delivery plan, build commitment across business functions and make sound decisions when priorities shift.
 
You will also bring:
  • Strong project governance skills, including integrated planning, risk management, assurance and executive reporting.
  • Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and influencing stakeholders across an organisation.
  • Financial and commercial capability, including budget management, forecasting, procurement and supplier coordination.
  • Clear communication, negotiation and problem-solving skills.
  • Practical knowledge of WHS, privacy, records management and operational compliance.
  • A relevant tertiary qualification or an equivalent combination of expertise and senior project experience.
  • A current Queensland driver licence and willingness to complete a National Police Check.
Experience in community housing, human services, property development, construction handover or asset management would be valuable. Experience opening new residential properties or services, implementing systems or managing data migration would also be well regarded.
 
What's on offer
  • Full-time hours, 38 hours per week.
  • A broad leadership role with autonomy and visibility across the organisation.
  • The opportunity to shape how new housing and services are brought into operation.
  • Work that contributes to safe, secure and affordable homes.

job.title: Senior Project Manager
job.description:
Inner Melbourne | $70M–$120M Projects | Tier 2 / Major Commercial Builder

An established and highly regarded Melbourne commercial builder is looking to appoint an experienced Senior Project Manager to take ownership of a major $70M–$120M multi-residential / student accommodation project in Inner Melbourne.
This is an opportunity to join a builder with a strong pipeline of complex projects and an established client base, working on a high-profile development where strong project leadership, commercial acumen and stakeholder management will be critical.

The Opportunity
You will take a senior leadership position within the project team, overseeing the project from procurement and early works through to completion and handover.
The project is a substantial multi-storey residential development and student accommodation project, requiring a highly experienced Project Manager who is comfortable managing complex construction environments, large subcontractor packages and significant project teams.
You will work closely with the Construction Manager, Site Manager, Contract Administrators, consultants, subcontractors and client to ensure the project is delivered safely, commercially and to the required quality and programme.

Key Responsibilities
  • Take overall responsibility for the successful delivery of $70M–$120M multi-residential / student accommodation projects
  • Lead and mentor the project team across construction, commercial, procurement and administration
  • Develop and manage the overall project programme, procurement strategy and delivery methodology
  • Oversee subcontractor procurement, tendering, negotiations and package awards
  • Manage project costs, budgets, forecasting and commercial performance
  • Take ownership of variations, EOTs, claims, extensions and contractual matters
  • Maintain strong relationships with the client, consultants, architects and key stakeholders
  • Lead design coordination and resolve technical/design issues throughout delivery
  • Work closely with site teams to manage sequencing, logistics, quality and programme
  • Identify project risks and implement mitigation strategies
  • Drive project safety, quality and compliance standards
  • Manage reporting to senior management and the client
  • Ensure project milestones, programme and commercial targets are achieved
  • Lead the project through to completion, defects and final handover
About You
We are looking for an experienced Senior Project Manager who has a proven track record delivering large-scale multi-residential, student accommodation, build-to-rent, hotel or similarly complex commercial projects.

Ideally, you will have:
  • 10+ years' construction experience, with significant PM experience
  • Proven delivery experience on projects valued at $70M+
  • Strong multi-residential or high-density residential experience
  • Student accommodation, build-to-rent, hotel or large-scale apartment experience highly regarded
  • Experience managing complex projects with multiple basements and significant structural packages
  • Strong knowledge of procurement, programming and subcontractor management
  • Excellent commercial and contractual understanding
  • Strong client and consultant management skills
  • Experience leading project teams and mentoring junior staff
  • Strong understanding of construction methodology and sequencing
  • Excellent communication and negotiation skills
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in Construction Management, Building, Engineering or a related discipline
The Builder
You will be joining an established Tier 2 / major commercial construction business with a strong reputation for delivering complex projects across Melbourne.
The business has an established pipeline across multi-residential, student accommodation, commercial and other large-scale developments, with a focus on quality delivery and long-term client relationships.
This is not a business where you will simply be another number on a major project. The successful candidate will have genuine responsibility for delivery and will work closely with senior leadership.

Why Join?
  • Work on a $70M–$120M landmark Inner Melbourne project
  • Strong pipeline of future projects
  • Established and respected commercial builder
  • Exposure to complex multi-residential and student accommodation construction
  • Genuine senior leadership opportunity
  • High level of project ownership and autonomy
  • Opportunity to work alongside an experienced construction team
  • Long-term career progression
  • Competitive salary package based on experience
Interested? If you're an experienced Senior Project Manager with a background in large-scale apartments, student accommodation, BTR or complex commercial construction, we'd like to hear from you.

  • Trade Coordination — Keep trades moving and maintain finishing schedules.
  • Client Handover — Deliver a smooth, well‑presented handover experience.
  • Site Safety — Maintain safe, tidy sites during the finishing phase.

What You’ll Bring
  • Experience in finishing, maintenance, or site supervision within residential construction.
  • Understanding of steel‑frame construction (preferred but not essential).

  • Ability to juggle multiple metro sites with both residential and small commercial components.

job.description:

For a Senior Estimator, there is the opportunity to step into a leadership role, while experienced Estimating Managers can step straight into the position and take ownership of the estimating function.

Working closely with the Operations, Sales and Construction teams, you will play an important role in managing the estimating process across a range of residential projects.


Key responsibilities will include:
  • Preparing and reviewing detailed residential estimates and quotations

  • Reviewing subcontractor and supplier pricing
  • Preparing and reviewing variations
  • Maintaining accurate pricing, product data and estimating information
  • Identifying and resolving discrepancies through analysis and problem-solving

  • Supporting and mentoring other members of the estimating team
  • Reviewing and improving estimating processes and systems
  • Producing reports and maintaining accurate project and pricing data
About You

We’re looking for someone with:
  • Previous experience in residential estimating, ideally within a custom or project homebuilder
  • Strong understanding of residential construction, pricing and building processes
  • Ability to read and interpret residential construction drawings and documentation
  • Strong experience with quantity take-offs, estimating and pricing
  • Strong attention to detail and organisational skills
  • Good commercial awareness and problem-solving ability
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to work across multiple teams
  • Experience managing or mentoring estimators would be advantageous
  • A proactive, reliable and self-motivated approach
  • Experience with estimating or construction management software
This is a great opportunity for someone who wants to step up into leadership, or for an existing Estimating Manager looking for a new challenge, with the opportunity to have genuine input into the estimating function and wider business.
